svg.text: Three learning signals: answers, structure, a score

g.text: Supervised learning
Signal: every example comes with the answer
(this email is "spam/normal")
Question: given a new example, what is the answer?
Typical: classification, prediction, translation
Cost: labels take people, money, time
Weakness: only answers "seen before"
questions; new situations derail it
Unsupervised learning
Signal: no answers, only the data itself
(ten thousand emails, none labelled)
Question: what shape does the data itself have?
Typical: clustering, dimensionality reduction, anomaly finding
Cost: hard to score whether the result is any good
Weakness: the "structure" it finds need not be
the structure you wanted
Reinforcement learning
Signal: no answers, only a score
(how the whole game went after this move)
Question: what action comes next?
Typical: chess, robotics, scheduling
Cost: trial and error needs a real environment and real stakes
Weakness: the score is late and sparse, so
"was this step good or bad" is hard to attribute

svg.text: One ruler: ask "what you hold while learning"——answers (supervised), data alone (unsupervised), a score alone (reinforcement).
